How to Guide - Build Your Open Engine:
https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/...

Your AI agents don't talk to each other, so you have become the human glue moving work between Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT. Open Engine is a shared task queue that lets your agents hand off work, carry the sources, and leave a receipt, without you stuck in the middle.

My Links 🔗
👉🏻 Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/
👉🏻 X: https://x.com/natebjones
👉🏻 TikTok:   / nate.b.jones  
👉🏻 Instagram:   / nate.b.jones  

What's really happening inside the AI agent coordination problem in 2026?

The common story is that agents go autonomous and take work off your plate. The real bottleneck is the handoff between agents, where the context, the sources, and the review keep falling on you.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on Open Engine, a practical way to get your agents working as one system:

Why the handoff, not the model, is the real bottleneck
How a shared queue lets agents pass work without you
What changes when you move from prompt mode to work mode
How agents from different tools coordinate without direct integration

The agents are finally capable enough to do the work, and the win now is building the queue that moves it between them before you become the bottleneck.

text:
SKILL DOWNLOAD: https://brad-b.kit.com/0b31eb2b33
WORK WITH ME: https://cal.com/bradley-bonanno/ai-st...
CONNECT WITH ME:   / bradbonanno  

For the last few months I've been running a sales research skill by hand every time a call books onto my calendar. It pulls the prospect's LinkedIn, work history, company size, recent news, open roles and buying signals so I walk into every call prepared. The problem is I have to remember to type slash research every single time, and on a busy morning I forget. In this video I take myself completely out of the loop and automate the whole thing inside my AIOS, so the research fires the instant a booking is made and the notes land on the calendar invite before I've even opened my laptop.

This is an unedited live build, bugs and all. I map out exactly what the agent (I call her Sally) needs to find and which tools get it there: Apify for LinkedIn scraping and Google search, Firecrawl for website and web search, and the Google Drive and Google Calendar MCPs to write a private research doc and attach it to the invite. Then I walk through the real architecture decision: why a local routine isn't event-based enough, and when to reach for a Claude cloud routine versus a managed agent. The trigger is a cal.com webhook, with make.com as the middleware that enriches the booking and fires the routine.

The second half is the hands-on wiring. I let Claude configure the cloud routine for me straight from the Git-tracked AIOS repo, set least-access permissions, and connect make.com to the routine's API trigger, including a few authentication mistakes I debug live (yes, I forgot the bearer prefix). I close by booking a test call as Tim Cook and watching the full chain run end to end: research scraped, private Google Doc created, attached to the calendar invite, and the executive brief committed back into the prospects folder in GitHub. I also flag the prompt-injection risk that free-text booking fields open up, and why hardening matters before this goes live. Whether you're a solo operator or building this out for a team, this is the blueprint for turning a manual skill into something that runs itself.

title: How to Create a Karpathy LLM Wiki for your Notes
text:
If you've been watching some of the recent discussions on AI and LLMs creating linked notes then you might be interested in Karpathy's ideas regarding building an automated, evolving LLM Wiki automatically using tools like Claude Code or Google Antigravity. In this video I show you the basics on getting started for how you might try to do this and examples with Obsidian and Apple Notes. #karpathy  #llmwiki #applenotes #obsidian
